chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ali ibn Khalid reported to me from Zaid ibn al-Husayn al-Kufi, who reported from Ja'far ibn Nujayh, who reported from Jandal ibn Waliq al-Taghlabi, who reported from Muhammad ibn Umar al-Mazini, from Abu Zaid al-Ansari, from Sa'id ibn Bashir, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, who said:
I heard a man asking Ibn Abbas about Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him.

Ibn Abbas told him: "Surely, Ali ibn Abi Talib prayed towards both Qiblas and swore allegiance on both occasions. He never worshipped an idol nor a graven image, and never cast lots upon his head with a divining arrow or a cup. He was born upon the natural disposition (fitrah), and did not associate any partner with Allah, even for the blink of an eye."

The man said: "I did not ask you about this. Rather, I asked you about his carrying his sword upon his shoulder, strutting proudly with it until he came to Basra and killed forty thousand therein, then marched to Syria and met the leaders of the Arabs, pitting some against others until he killed them, then came to Nahrawan while they were Muslims and killed them to the last one."

Ibn Abbas said to him: "Is Ali more knowledgeable in your view, or I?" He said: "If Ali had been more knowledgeable in my view than you, I would not have asked you!" He said: Ibn Abbas became so enraged that his anger intensified.

Then he said: "May your mother mourn you! Ali taught me. His knowledge was from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, was taught by Allah from above His Throne. So the knowledge of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace, is from Allah, and Ali's knowledge is from the Prophet, and my knowledge is from Ali's knowledge, and the knowledge of all the companions of Muhammad, compared to Ali's knowledge, peace be upon him, is like a single drop in seven oceans."

key_terms.البيعتين: The two pledges of allegiance: likely referring to the First and Second Pledges of Aqabah or the pledge at Ghadir Khumm.
key_terms.الفطرة: Fitrah: the innate, natural disposition toward monotheism with which every human is born.
key_terms.القبلتين: The two Qiblas: Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis) and Mecca (al-Ka'bah). Ali prayed toward both before and after the change of Qibla direction.
key_terms.كالقطرة الواحدة في سبعة أبحر: Like a single drop in seven oceans: a powerful metaphor for the incomparable vastness of Ali's knowledge.

ai.seo_question: What did Ibn Abbas say about Imam Ali's knowledge compared to the other companions?
ai.summary: In this exchange recorded by Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, a man questions Ibn Abbas about Imam Ali's role in the battles of Basra (Jamal), Siffin (Syria), and Nahrawan. Rather than responding to the political accusations, Ibn Abbas passionately declares Ali's chain of knowledge: Ali learned from the Prophet (SAWW), who learned from Allah. He concludes that all the knowledge of the Prophet's companions combined is merely a drop compared to Ali's knowledge, which is like seven oceans.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 6. He said: Abul Hasan ‘Ali ibn Khalid reported to me from Zaid ibn al-Husayn al-Kufi, who reported from Ja’far ibn Nujayh, who reported from Jandal ibn Waliq al-Taghlabi, who reported from Muhammad ibn Umar al-Mazini, from Abu Zaid al-Ansari, from Saeed ibn Bashir, from Qutadah, from Saeed ibn al-Musayyib, who said:
I heard a man ask Ibn Abbas about ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him.

Ibn Abbas told him: "Surely, ‘Ali is the one who prayed towards both the Qiblas and swore allegiance to the Prophet on both occassions. He never worshipped an idol nor did he divine by the arrows. He was born a Muslim and did not associate any partner to Him, even for a wink."

The man said: "I did not ask you that! I want to know from you about the sword which he proudly carried over his shoulder, came to Basrah and killed forty thousand. Then he went to Syria, confronted the Arab leaders, pitting one against the other and then killed them. Then he came to Nahrawan and killed the Muslims upto the last one."

Ibn Abbas told him: "Who do you think is more knowledgeable, ‘Ali or myself?" He said: "If I had thought ‘Ali to be more knowledgeable, I would not have come to you!" Upon hearing this, Ibn Abbas was enraged

and he said: "May your mother mourn you! ‘Ali is the one who taught me. And his knowledge is from the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, and the Prophet received knowledge from Allah, Most High. So, the knowledge of the Prophet is from Allah, and ‘Ali’s knowledge is from the Prophet and my knowledge is from ‘Ali. And the knowledge of all the companions of Muhammad, peace be upon him and his progeny, when compared to ‘Ali’s knowledge is just like a drop in the seven oceans."
